blocks.content: A Kubernetes Volume is storage attached directly to a Pod, as briefly introduced in the What is a Pod topic. This broader Volume concept covers several types, most tied to the Pod's own lifecycle, not independently persistent the way the PV/PVC system covered later in this module is.

Kubernetes supports a range of Pod-level volume types: emptyDir (temporary scratch space), hostPath (a path on the node itself), configMap and secret (covered in the Configuration module), and various cloud-specific disk types.

blocks.alt: A range of volume types, each serving a different purpose

blocks.content: This is the key distinction from what is covered later in this module: most ordinary Volumes survive a container restarting within the same Pod (exactly as covered in the Pod Lifecycle topic), but do not survive the Pod itself being deleted.

blocks.alt: Surviving a container restart, but not surviving the Pod's own deletion

blocks.content: emptyDir creates an empty directory when the Pod starts, useful for temporary data or scratch space shared between containers in the same Pod, and it is deleted entirely the moment the Pod is removed, exactly what its name suggests.

blocks.alt: Truly temporary, gone the instant the Pod itself is gone

blocks.content: hostPath mounts a path directly from the node's own filesystem into the Pod, this is genuinely useful in specific cases, but risky in general, since it ties the Pod to whatever happens to be on that specific node, breaking the portability Kubernetes otherwise provides.

blocks.alt: A direct shortcut to the node's own disk, with real portability tradeoffs

blocks.content: 5. Where the More Advanced Storage Lives
blocks.text: 5. Where the More Advanced Storage Lives

blocks.content: For storage that genuinely needs to outlive any individual Pod, the Persistent Volume and Persistent Volume Claim system, covered in the next two topics, is the right tool, a meaningfully more capable and durable mechanism than ordinary Pod-level Volumes.

blocks.alt: A more advanced, genuinely persistent mechanism, covered starting next

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Kubernetes Volume is Pod-attached storage of several possible types, most tied to the Pod's own lifecycle, surviving a container restart but not Pod deletion.
emptyDir is genuine scratch space, hostPath is a risky direct shortcut to the node's disk, neither is meant for data that needs to outlive the Pod, that is what PV/PVC is for.
